subject: Aurora Cloud - sudden throughput regression & elevated 5xx/429
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@aurora-cloud.com>

Cc: Elena Morales <elena@aurora-cloud.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Elevated 5xx/429 and throughput drop - urgent

Hi Rachel,

We started seeing a sharp degradation in throughput this morning around 07:50 PST. Our clients are reporting elevated 5xx and 429 spikes and timeouts across several routes that hit the Redwood hosted endpoints. Error rates spiked from ~0.3% to ~6% and p95 latency jumped from 420ms to ~2.4s. We captured sample traces and a short batch of error responses (attached).

Can you confirm whether Redwood is doing any config changes, autoscaling events, or model variant fallbacks in us-west-2 this morning? We need an ETA for a mitigation path and I may need to brief our CTO and customer success leads shortly.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel

Subject: Re: Elevated 5xx/429 and throughput drop - urgent

Samir — thanks for the quick flag and the sample traces. I’m escalating to reliability and ops now. Initial quick checks: no deployments from Redwood control plane in us-west-2 since 06:30; autoscaler did trigger several GPU scale-outs between 07:10-07:30 but those completed. We are running an emergency diagnostic.

Immediate next steps we’re executing (I’ll update here as we confirm):
- Sean is validating routing and fallback policies (ensuring that requests aren’t being routed to a high-latency model variant).
- Marcus is pulling perf counters and KV cache hit rates to check for cache churn causing token backlog.
- We will enable a short-lived client-side 50rps rate limiter per-API-key (5 minutes window) for the worst-hit routes to break retry amplification while we stabilize.
- We’ll prepare a customer-facing status update for the Redwood status page and coordinate messaging with Aurora.

ETA for a first mitigation window: 30–45 minutes. I’ll post the status page draft for your review in 15 minutes.

— Rachel

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Elevated 5xx/429 and throughput drop - urgent

Quick findings from the diagnostics:
- We observed a sudden KV cache eviction spike coincident with a large prefix flood from a small subset of Aurora keys; cache hit rate on the affected shard dropped from 88% -> 27%.
- Two model nodes in the pool started reporting transient OOMs which led to request retries; autoscaler added capacity but the retry amplification outpaced the scale-up window.
- Route-level tokenization showed anomalous long-context requests (avg seq length jumped 4x) causing higher per-request resource usage.

Mitigations applied (09:00–09:20 PST):
- Enabled per-API-key circuit breaker for three affected routes (fail-fast 503 after 3 attempts) to prevent retries from backfilling the queue.
- Rebalanced KV cache shard assignments to protect hot prefixes and warmed a fast-path cache snapshot for Aurora’s top 10 keys.
- Temporarily pinned Aurora traffic to a smaller, stable model variant with shorter max-context to reduce per-request cost.

Impact so far: error rates dropped from 6% -> 1.4% and p95 latency improved to ~850ms. We’re still seeing intermittent 429s during bursts.

Next steps: continue soak; Marcus to dive deeper on the OOM root cause and whether tokenization settings should be constrained upstream. We should coordinate the customer-facing ETA once we confirm sustained improvement.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Elevated 5xx/429 and throughput drop - urgent

Samir / Elena —

Thanks for your patience. Short customer-facing summary (we will also post this on Redwood status and link to the incident page):

What happened: A sudden workload pattern change from Aurora produced a short-lived meta-pattern of long-context requests and hot prefix traffic that triggered large KV cache evictions and transient OOMs on two model nodes. The resulting retries and queue buildup caused a spike in 5xx/429 and higher latencies.

What we did:
- Applied per-API-key circuit breakers and short-lived rate limits to break retry amplification.
- Rebalanced and warmed KV caches; pinned Aurora traffic to a lower-context model variant and scale-rebalanced the node pool.
- Engineers mitigated the OOM path and removed a memory regression introduced in a non-critical optimization layer.

Current status: Stabilized with error rate now ~0.9% and p95 ~630ms. We recommend Aurora apply a short client-side guard (limit context length to the pre-change median where possible) while we roll a targeted fix. Estimated completion for the permanent fix and postmortem: 48 hours.

Action items for Aurora:
- Short-term: throttle the largest clients or reduce max tokens for critical routes for 24h.
- Medium-term: share a representative prompt set (anonymized) so our model-ops team can reproduce the context pattern and tune quantization/eviction heuristics.

If you want a joint exec sync, Laura (VP CS) and I are available at 16:00 PT today for a 30-minute brief with your CTO. Please confirm.

Best,
